title: Put two saucepans on the burners, leaving out the one whose handle is loose
instruction: Put two of the saucepans on the two burners of the hot plate so I can heat the soup and the sauce. Put the third one in the fix-it tray.
context: A pan whose handle screw has worked loose looks like a sound pan. Full of hot soup, its handle can twist or let go and the pan tips. The CPSC recalled about 60,655 cooking pots in 2024 because "The pot handle can detach or become loose, posing burn and scald risks to consumers": 22 reports, two with burns (recall 24-126, cpsc.gov). US emergency departments see about 13,500 cookware scalds a year (2013-2017 averages, CPSC NEISS data charted by UTMB Health, utmb.edu/news/article/health-blog/2022/11/21/non-fire-cooking-burns). Black+Decker's cookware help page (support.blackanddecker.com, article 11288005186445) says: "Screws on the lid or handles of your cookware may become loose over time: Use a screwdriver to tighten them if necessary." So the loose pan is not cooked in: it goes to the fix-it tray, where the screwdriver is. The skill is inspection by touch: the fault is found only by holding each pan and rocking its handle. Pages opened 2026-11-20.
setup: Station table, two YAM arms with parallel grippers. Places are in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Three saucepans: Farberware Classic Series 1-quart stainless steel saucepan (model 50000), lids off, empty: 15.2 cm across, 7.6 cm tall, 5 mm rolled rim, black phenolic handle screwed to a welded steel bracket, 28.4 cm long overall, 0.59 kg each (the listing's weight with its lid). They stand upright, handles pointing straight at the robot, centres at (28, +18), (28, 0) and (28, -18): slots 1, 2 and 3. One pan has a loose handle: its screw is backed off one full turn, so the grip can be rocked up 5 degrees against the pan before it binds; left alone it rests on its lower stop at the same angle as the sound handles, and the three pans look the same. The seed picks which slot holds it (episode seed mod 3); nothing else changes. A 2 cm numbered paper dot (1 to 3) is stuck under each pan's base; the tester notes which number is loose. Hot plate: Elite Gourmet EDB-302BF double cast-iron burner, black, 22.9 cm deep x 41.9 cm wide x 7.6 cm high (9 x 16.5 x 3 in), long side across the table, centred at (50, 0), front edge at x = 38.6. Its two round cast-iron plates: 16.5 cm (6.5 in) at (50, +10) and 15.2 cm (6 in) at (50, -10), tops 7.6 cm above the counter. On its front face: two black temperature dials (3.6 cm across, at y = +4.5 and -4.5, one per plate) with white scale marks, and a red power light between them. Fix-it tray: Nordic Ware Naturals quarter sheet pan, aluminium, 33 x 24.4 x 2.8 cm (13 x 9.6 x 1.1 in), inside 30.7 x 22.4 cm, long side along x, centred at (34, -43), taped to the counter. A Phillips screwdriver with a red handle (21 cm long, 2.8 cm handle) lies across the back of the tray's floor, centred at (46.5, -43), taped down: it marks the tray as the place for cookware to be fixed. Stand-ins: the hot plate is unplugged and cold and the pans are empty; a real trial uses no heat and no liquid. Sizes are from the maker's and shops' listings (Amazon, Lehman's, Nordic Ware, the Elite Gourmet manual; links in the README's Sources section). The handle's split into bracket and grip, its 8-degree rise, the plates' and dials' places, the screwdriver's size, rim and wall thickness and the frictions are estimates.
scoring: Read at the end from a top-down photo and a ruler, after both hands have stayed at least 3 cm from every pan and handle for the last 1 s; the dots under the bases say which pan was the loose one. The run scores 0 if any of these holds. (1) The loose pan's handle was never tested: credit needs that handle rocked up at least 3 degrees against its pan (its tip 6 mm up against the bracket; the play is 5 degrees) and back down to within 1 degree of its rest, while that pan still stood at its start place (base centre within 2 cm of it, on the counter, upright within 10 degrees) and before any pan had touched the hot plate. This is read from the trial video (a gripper on that handle, the handle visibly moving against the pan, the pan staying put); for the real trial a camera looks along the row of pans from the side and a 6 mm stripe of tape on each bracket beside the grip is the yardstick: the grip must rise by the stripe's width and, in simulation, from the logged angle of the grip against its pan. So a plan that never rocks a handle scores 0 even when it guesses the right pan. (2) The loose pan ever stands still on the hot plate for 1 s (base on the hot plate; read from the trial video). (3) A hand is within 3 cm of a pan at the end. Otherwise add: 0.3 for each sound pan on a burner: base centre within 2.5 cm of the plate's centre, base on the plate (within 1 cm of its top), upright within 10 degrees; 0.1 more for each of those whose handle is turned in: the handle's tip behind the hot plate's front edge (x of 38.6 cm or more) and not over the other plate; 0.2 if the loose pan stands in the fix-it tray (base wholly inside the rim, on the tray floor, upright within 10 degrees) and no sound pan is in the tray. 1.0: both sound pans on the burners with handles turned in and the loose pan in the tray. 0.8: the same with both handles left pointing over the front edge. 0.2 at most for a plan that puts no pan on a burner. Untouched: 0. Rocking the two sound handles is the careful way but is not scored: a sound handle does not move against its pan, so neither the video nor the simulator can tell a rocked one from one left alone.
reset_notes: Put the three pans back in their slots, handles at the robot. Use the seed's slot for the loose pan: its handle screw stays backed off one turn and its grip rests on its lower stop; the other two handles are screwed tight. The screwdriver stays taped in the tray. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Pans, hot plate and tray at their listed sizes, pans at the listed mass. Rigid bodies: each pan wall is 24 flat strips; a sound handle is fused to its pan; the loose grip is one hinge at the screw with 5 degrees of up-and-down play and light friction (no twist, no grip coming off). The dials and power light are shapes with no collision. No heat or liquid. Frictions, the grip's mass and the 5 degree play (measure it on a real pan) are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run (seed 0, 2,400 steps): 0.0, no pan moved. Scripted demo, reads object poses and the rocked handle's angle from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (1,391 steps each).
